item.title: Sony and Mitsubishi Set Up AI Vision Joint Venture for Factories
item.description: Mitsubishi Electric Corp. and Sony Group Corp. said they will set up a joint venture to provide factory automation services by combining their expertise in artificial intelligence and image sensors.

item.title: China’s ‘AI for All’ Offensive Defies US Containment Playbook
item.description: The rapidly increasing global competitiveness of China’s artificial intelligence models is ringing alarm bells in Washington, posing a new test for the standard protectionist playbook.

item.title: Rising Crude, US Rate-Hike Bets Counter Dollar Inflow Support for Rupee
item.description: The Indian currency has fallen about 2% from its June high.

item.title: Sri Lanka Holds Rates as US-Iran War Clouds Economic Outlook
item.description: Sri Lanka’s central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, balancing the need to bring inflation back to target while supporting economic growth as renewed conflict between the US and Iran clouds the global outlook.

item.title: PHP/USD: Philippine Peso Declines to Match Record Low on Higher Oil Prices
item.description: The Philippine peso dropped to match the record low as higher oil prices put pressure on the currency.

item.title: High-Risk Bets That Burned Korean Traders Are Making a Comeback
item.description: South Korea’s risk-loving retail investors are flocking to a leveraged instrument that has inflicted severe losses in the past, adding to concerns about abrupt unwinding of wagers as the stock market gyrates.

item.title: RBA Survey Shows Inflation Remains Top Concern for Australians
item.description: Australia’s central bank said results from a new survey showed inflation was the top economic concern for respondents, adding “fundamental gaps” remain in the public’s understanding of how monetary policy works.

item.title: Korean Stocks Jump as Brokers Say Margin Unwind Nearing End
item.description: South Korean stocks jumped, as the unwinding of leveraged bets that helped drive the benchmark nearly 30% below its peak appeared to be nearing its end.

item.title: Blackstone Tying Up $3 Billion AirTrunk Loan as Data Center Debt Binge Woes Grow
item.description: Blackstone Inc. is finalizing a group of banks to underwrite a A$4.3 billion ($3 billion) loan for the construction of AirTrunk Pty.’s new data center in Australia, according to people familiar with the matter, despite growing worries over the massive debt racked up for artificial intelligence infrastructure projects.

item.title: Katayama Warns of Bold Action as Yen Slides Past 163 Per Dollar
item.description: Two senior Japanese officials warned that authorities are ready to take action in the currency market if necessary, in comments that did little to support the beleaguered yen.

item.title: Indian Rupee Rebound Bets Vanish as Soaring Crude Blunts Inflows
item.description: With oil prices on the ascent again, bets that tens of billions of dollars in fresh capital inflows would sustain a recovery in the Indian rupee have all but vanished.

item.title: EUR/CNY: Why China’s Yuan Is Drawing Scrutiny in Europe, What It Means for Euro
item.description: The value of the yuan has become a flashpoint in trade relations between China and the European Union. Many EU policymakers and economists believe the currency is undervalued and a key driver of the bloc’s deepening trade deficit with the East Asian nation. That imbalance averaged about $1.1 billion a day in June.

item.title: Hong Kong Brokers Cling to Lunch Break Exchange Wants to Scrap
item.description: Thousands of stock traders, brokers and other financial professionals in Hong Kong may soon lose their lunch hour — and some aren’t happy about it.

item.title: Thai Bonds Are Beating Asia and Analysts Predict Further Gains
item.description: Thailand’s bonds have beaten their emerging Asian peers over the past month and analysts predict they will extend gains on favorable supply dynamics and slower inflation.

item.title: Indonesia Seen Hiking Rate in Close Call, Putting Rupiah Ahead of Slowing Growth
item.description: A narrow majority of economists expect Bank Indonesia to raise interest rates again to support the rupiah and contain inflation, even as the economy slows.

item.title: Japan’s Trade Deficit Widens as Yen, Iran War Inflate Imports
item.description: Japan’s trade deficit unexpectedly widened in June as the weak yen inflated the value of imports and the war in Iran made oil more expensive.

item.title: Gold Holds Gain as Traders Weigh Impact of Oil Risks on Rates
item.description: Gold held a gain as traders monitored threats to energy supply routes that risk stoking inflation and putting pressure on the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates.

item.title: Innolight Seeks Up to $7 Billion in Biggest Hong Kong Listing in Years
item.description: China’s Zhongji Innolight Co. has started taking investor orders for a Hong Kong listing to raise as much as HK$55 billion ($7 billion), the city’s biggest in seven years.

item.title: Newborn Town Targets Global Viewers With AI-Made Short Dramas
item.description: Chinese social networking and entertainment provider Newborn Town Inc. is doubling down on artificial intelligence to create short dramas in a bet the technology can slash costs while fueling growth across emerging markets.

item.title: Yen Slides Past 163 Mark to Fresh Four-Decade Low Against Dollar
item.description: The yen slid past 163 per dollar for the first time since 1986, extending its decline and increasingly testing Japanese authorities’ resolve to intervene.

item.title: KKR Commercial Real Estate Lender Studies Potential Sale, Merger
item.description: A commercial real estate lender managed by KKR & Co. said it’s considering strategic alternatives that could include a merger or sale of the money-losing company.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 22
item.description: Oil edged higher after President Donald Trump played down the prospect of near-term talks with Iran while threatening further strikes, as risks to global supply spread beyond the Middle East to the Black Sea.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set to Rise on Tech Rally, Oil Gains: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were set for a second day of gains as a rebound in chipmakers at the heart of the artificial intelligence boom offset concerns over renewed escalation in the US-Iran conflict.

item.title: Hong Kong Home Prices Set for 19% Rebound Over Two Years: BI
item.description: Hong Kong home prices are expected to rebound the most in nearly a decade in 2026, driven by strong mainland Chinese demand, limited supply and robust rental growth, according to Bloomberg Intelligence.

item.title: Banks Wrap Up Loan Backing SoftBank’s $5.4 Billion Robotics Bet
item.description: A group of banks wrapped up a loan offering backing SoftBank Group Corp.’s $5.4 billion robotics bet after increasing the size of the US dollar tranche.

item.title: This ETF Tax Loophole Is All the Rage Among Rich Americans
item.description: A bespoke fund is becoming a must-have tool for wealthy investors looking to defer — and sometimes even avoid — capital gains tax.

item.title: Nintendo Scores Hit With Tomodachi Life as Gamers Seek Escape With Life Sims
item.description: Six years after Nintendo Co.’s Animal Crossing: New Horizons became a lockdown phenomenon, the company is scoring another major hit worldwide from gamers seeking an escape from rising anxiety and isolation.

item.title: Moody’s Lifts Argentina Debt Rating in Fresh Boost to Milei
item.description: Moody’s Ratings upgraded Argentina’s credit score, giving the nation its third sovereign upgrade in less than three months and further validating President Javier Milei’s economic overhaul plan.

item.title: Alaska Airlines Narrowly Beats Estimates as Fuel Costs Stay High
item.description: Alaska Air Group Inc. earnings outlook slightly beat analyst predictions as the airline grapples with rising fuel prices from the war in the Middle East.

item.title: Super Micro Jumps After Early Results Show Rising Backlog
item.description: Super Micro Computer Inc. shares rose about 15% in extended trading after the server maker issued preliminary results saying its backlog hit a record on new orders in the quarter of more than $60 billion.
